titulo: Their clock, and why eating early costs you the good table
subtitulo: A restaurant serving dinner at six in a tourist centre is telling you who it is for — the same kitchen at half eight is a different room
cena: It is quarter past six, you are hungry, and the only place with the lights on has a menu in four languages outside.
frasePiso: Ask what time they start. The answer tells you both when to eat and what kind of place you are standing in front of.
decisao: esperar até as oito e meia e jantar onde os locais jantam, em vez de comer às seis na casa que só vive de turista

steps.pt: Italy runs on a later clock than most visitors arrive with, and the gap between the two is where the tourist trap lives.

steps.acao: Note the hour and come back then. Do not sit down two hours early somewhere else.
steps.es: La cucina apre alle otto. Prima solo aperitivo.
steps.pt: The kitchen opens at eight. Before that, only aperitivo.
steps.tts: La cucina apre alle otto. Prima solo aperitivo.

steps.promptPt: Ask what time the kitchen opens. Speak now.
steps.es: A che ora apre la cucina?
steps.pinyin: a keh O-ra A-pre la koo-CHEE-na
steps.pt: What time does the kitchen open?
steps.tts: A che ora apre la cucina?

steps.pt: Dinner service generally starts around half seven or eight, later in the south, and the room fills after nine rather than at opening.

steps.promptPt: Book a table for the hour locals eat, not the hour you are hungry. Speak now.
steps.es: Un tavolo per due alle nove, è possibile?
steps.pinyin: oon TA-vo-lo per DOO-eh AL-le NO-ve, eh pos-SEE-bee-le
steps.pt: A table for two at nine, is that possible?
steps.tts: Un tavolo per due alle nove, è possibile?

steps.pt: So what do you do with the two hours? What everyone else does: the aperitivo you learned in the last part.

steps.promptPt: Lunch has its own window. Ask until when they serve it. Speak now.
steps.es: Fino a che ora si pranza?
steps.pinyin: FEE-no a keh O-ra see PRAN-tsa
steps.pt: Until what time do you serve lunch?
steps.tts: Fino a che ora si pranza?

steps.acao: Half past two is the hard edge. After it the kitchen is closed, not slow.
steps.es: Fino alle due e mezza. Poi la cucina chiude.
steps.pt: Until half past two. Then the kitchen closes.
steps.tts: Fino alle due e mezza. Poi la cucina chiude.

steps.pt: A place serving full dinners at six in a tourist centre is not wrong. It is telling you who its customers are.

steps.promptPt: Ask someone local where they eat, not where you should eat. Speak now.
steps.es: Lei dove va a mangiare la sera?
steps.pinyin: lay DO-ve va a man-JA-re la SE-ra
steps.pt: Where do you go to eat in the evening?
steps.tts: Lei dove va a mangiare la sera?

steps.pt: That wording matters. Where should I eat gets you the tourist answer; where do you eat gets you the other one.

steps.promptPt: Ask whether you need to book at all. Speak now.
You did not book and it is nine o'clock. Ask, using the frame from B08. Speak now.
steps.pt: Is there a place without a booking?

steps.promptPt: It is late and you want to know if you still have time. Speak now.
steps.es: Siamo ancora in tempo per mangiare?
steps.pinyin: SYA-mo an-KO-ra een TEM-po per man-JA-re
steps.pt: Are we still in time to eat?
steps.tts: Siamo ancora in tempo per mangiare?

steps.promptPt: Book for tomorrow while you are standing there. Speak now.
steps.pt: Then I'll book for tomorrow evening.

steps.es: A che ora apre la cucina? Un tavolo per due alle nove, è possibile? Lei dove va a mangiare la sera?
steps.pinyin: a keh O-ra A-pre la koo-CHEE-na. oon TA-vo-lo per DOO-eh AL-le NO-ve eh pos-SEE-bee-le. lay DO-ve va a man-JA-re la SE-ra
steps.pt: Shadow the three questions that fix your evening.
steps.tts: A che ora apre la cucina? Un tavolo per due alle nove, è possibile? Lei dove va a mangiare la sera?

steps.pt: I01 done. Kitchen hours, a table at nine, and lei dove va — the wording that gets the real answer.

secoes.corpo: Kitchens generally serve lunch from around half twelve to half two and then stop entirely. Arriving at three expecting a full meal is the single most common way visitors end up eating badly.

exemplos.es: Fino a che ora si pranza?
exemplos.pt: Until what time do you serve lunch?

exemplos.es: Siamo ancora in tempo per mangiare?
exemplos.pt: Are we still in time to eat?

secoes.corpo: In the north a kitchen may open at half seven; in the south nine is ordinary and the room can fill at ten. Worth being honest about the status of these numbers: opening hours were fully deregulated in 2011, so none of this is a rule, and no national survey of when Italians actually sit down was findable. It is a well-reported convention, not a measurement — which is exactly why the part teaches you to ask rather than to memorise a clock.

A full dinner service at six in a central tourist area is not a scam, it is a business decision about who walks past. It usually comes with a multilingual menu and photographs, which is the same signal repeated.
Dove dovrei mangiare invites a recommendation calibrated for a visitor. Lei dove va a mangiare asks about their own life and produces a different list, usually further from the centre and cheaper.

permissao: You are allowed to be hungry for two hours. Waiting until half eight is not an endurance test with a cultural point to it — it is simply where the good tables are, and the aperitivo exists precisely to fill that gap.
espelho: Anyone who has eaten dinner at five on the first night of a trip because the body clock had not moved yet knows this gap. It closes by itself in two days; the only cost is which restaurants you saw in the meantime.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You walk past a restaurant at eight in the evening and it is almost empty, so you assume it is not good and keep walking.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: An empty room at dinner time means locals avoid this place.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: Eight is early for dinner in most of Italy and very early in the south. The room you are judging fills between nine and ten, and the emptiness you are reading as a verdict is just the hour.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Ask a che ora apre la cucina, book for nine, and go and have an aperitivo in between.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You stop selecting restaurants by which ones are full of people on a foreign schedule, which is a filter that reliably picks the wrong ones.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not at lunch, where a full room genuinely is a good sign because the window is narrow and everyone eats within the same two hours — and not in a place that is empty at ten.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: There is no legally fixed dinner hour in Italy: opening and closing times for commercial and food-service businesses were fully liberalised by Art. 31 of D.L. 201/2011, converted into L. 214/2011, applying nationwide without regional implementation. The hours taught in this part are therefore convention rather than rule, and no Istat or trade survey of average dinner start times was locatable — the north-south gradient is widely reported but not measured.
fatosDatados.fonte: Camera dei Deputati — dossier «Disciplina degli orari di apertura degli esercizi commerciali»; D.L. 201/2011 conv. L. 214/2011
